articles.content:
Proton has fallen from grace... is it time to leave? Support my work or let me die: https://www.patreon.com/thehatedone

It feels like a lifetime ago. That time when I first signed up for Proton. It was called ProtonMail back then. And you had to get on a waiting list to open an account. Proton would always be a privacy-first company and nothing else.

It was this noble goal and humble origins that started ProtonMail. A company that would soon become an empire of its own. It took the crown of the largest alternative ecosystem of “privacy-first” apps. Mail, VPN, Drive, Calendar, Documents, Password Manager, authenticator, crypto wallet, AI chatbot… it’s hard to even count.

At least Proton wasn’t like the big tech. It was different. Because it wasn’t doing things like using your data for ads. Or shoving AI down everybody’s throat. Or unnecessarily engaging in partisan politics. And their CEO was a good guy. Unlike the sycophantic megalomaniac narcissistic personalities we grew accustomed to in the big tech.

Uh-oh…

Proton CEO Andy Yen is pushing AI so hard he set up a tattletale email address so that he can “ruthlessly smash everything that stands in the way of AI velocity”.

But using AI means relying on someone’s else’s platform to develop your product. The same platform that now thousands of other companies use to make their product as well. That platform is now a gatekeeper. If anyone wanted to compromise thousands of companies at once, this platform is a juicy target. Such attacks are not theoretical, they do happen in the wild.

Security is not the only casualty of Proton’s shift in priorities. On the long enough timeline, everything with a private for profit motive will go out of business, sell or enshittify. This constant drive for infinite growth is what ruins everything. I don’t trust that incentive at all.

Proton is grandstanding that their for-profit company is governed by a non-profit foundation. But it’s clearly not working to tame the for-profit beast because “insufficient velocity” and annual revenue is the reason we are here. It’s the reason Andy Yen felt entitled to act like a petulant child and bully his employees. And command his loyalists to go on Reddit and spam positivity in his favor.

articles.content:
Signal is doing too little, too late. F**k’em! Donate to me instead: https://www.patreon.com/thehatedone

NOTE: You can still use something and f*ck it at the same time.

Signal is disappointing. And I am tired of pretending that it’s not.
I have been using and recommending Signal for longer than it existed. Signal just came out with a feature we have been waiting for for 8 years.

You see 8 years ago, the only flaw Signal had was that it required a phone number to register and find contacts. This was bad, because it meant you couldn’t get an anonymous Signal account, which meant you could get hacked or abused by anyone who knew your phone number. It was also easy for authoritarians to censor people’s access to Signal by denying phone registrations by country code.

The reason for the phone number requirement was to prevent spam. The primary function, was to use your phonebook to quickly onboard new users and send notifications whenever anyone in your contact list signed up on Signal. A very convenient Silicon Valley feature that allowed people to quickly connect with their friends and also let domestic abusers find out their victims are trying to contact a lawyer’s office over Signal.
